about.title: Parlier Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Parlier residents rely on everyday products — farm equipment, kitchen appliances, tools, vehicle parts, children's items — without expecting them to fail. When a product does fail and someone gets hurt, California law often lets the injured person pursue the manufacturer, distributor, or retailer under strict liability, meaning the focus is on whether the product was defective, not whether anyone was careless. In a community like Parlier, where agricultural equipment and everyday household goods both see heavy use, defect claims can arise from a cracked housing, a missing warning label, or a manufacturing shortcut that never should have left the factory. If a defective product injured you or someone in your family here in Fresno County, the single most important step is holding onto the product exactly as it was at the time of the injury. We handle product liability claims on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to find out where you stand.

whyChoose.title: Why Strict Liability Matters in Parlier

items.title: You Don't Have to Prove Negligence
items.desc: Under California's strict liability rules, an injured person generally needs to show the product was defective and caused harm, not that the company was careless. That can simplify what you have to prove from the start.

items.title: Multiple Parties Can Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and even retailers who sold the defective product may all be held liable under California law. This gives us more than one avenue to pursue accountability on your behalf.

items.title: Preserving the Product Preserves Your Claim
items.desc: Because defect claims often hinge on physical evidence, keeping the product exactly as it was after the injury can matter a great deal. We can advise you on safely storing it before any inspection or testing takes place.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: No. California generally allows strict liability claims for defective products, which means the focus is on whether the product itself was flawed, not whether the company acted negligently. We can look at whether a design, manufacturing, or warning defect contributed to your injury.

items.question: What if the product was fixed or thrown away after I got hurt?
items.answer: It's best to keep the product in its post-injury condition if at all possible, since it's often central evidence in these claims. If it's already been discarded or repaired, don't worry — we can still discuss what other evidence, like receipts, photos, or medical records, might support your case.

items.question: Are product injuries common in a city like Parlier?
items.answer: Parlier sees a steady number of injury collisions and everyday incidents each year, and defective products can play a role in some of those, whether it's farm machinery, vehicle components, or household goods. Even in a smaller community, a faulty product can cause serious harm, and California law doesn't require a big city for a valid claim.

items.question: Does this cost anything upfront?
items.answer: Our case review is free, and we typically work on contingency, meaning we're only paid if you recover compensation. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with us.
